I can't advocate the expulsion of anyone from a university based on a belief. It's a place where intermingling among people from various walks of life with different perspectives come to exchange ideas, even if they might be misguided. I think the objective is to figure out a way to make the process accessible to these people without hindering the process itself. To me it is the difference between saying we should install ramps and elevators to make a campus accessible to the disabled, and saying that we should tear out all stairs and buildings over one story and make everyone use wheelchairs so as not to make disabled people feel bad.

If you refuse to take classes because they don't carry trigger warnings, then you deserve to be expelled. If you continuously make a scene because the courses don't include them, the college would be right to consider whether you were interfering with the other students' learning - and expel you if you were. If you genuinely have trouble taking the class due to actual PTSD issues, then it's likely you should choose another course or arrange an alternate way to take it if the college will allow.

In every case, one individual shouldn't be catered to at the expense of the rest.

I don't think we disagree; inclusion of my analogy was to exemplify the point of your last sentence. But I believe it is unfair to equate increasing accessibility to catering, especially if the means of increasing accessibility doesn't actually diminish the experience (in this case, the education) of others involved.

What I am fine with is the basic kind of "trigger warnings" we've had for years when you watch the news ("We want to warn you that the footage you're about to see is graphic and might be disturbing to some viewers"), and while attending university, our professors would provide similar verbal warnings if they showed a clip or a film that contained something graphic. It's courteous for those who give a shit, and despite being someone who didn't give a shit about how graphic something is, I did not feel put upon by the warning being provided.
